## Analysis

This PKGBUILD file is for the `penpot-mcp` package (along with related packages penpot, penpot-exporter, and penpot-frontend) and builds the Penpot open-source design tool from its official GitHub source.

**Source verification:** The primary source is downloaded from `https://github.com/penpot/penpot/archive/refs/tags/$pkgver.tar.gz`, which is the official Penpot GitHub repository. A SHA-256 checksum (`77f13869...`) is provided for this source. All other sources are local files included in the AUR repository itself, each with their own checksums. No external or untrusted download sources are used.

**Build process:** The `build()` function sets up standard build environments (Rust, Java, Node.js/pnpm) and invokes the upstream Penpot build scripts. It uses `sed` to patch upstream build scripts to use system-provided tools (e.g., replacing `/opt/emsdk/` with `/usr/lib/emsdk/`, patching Playwright to use system Chromium, removing corepack references). These are standard AUR packaging practices for ensuring builds use system libraries rather than downloading bundled binaries.

**Package functions:** The `package_*()` functions install compiled artifacts into standard Arch Linux paths (`$pkgdir/usr/share`, `$pkgdir/usr/lib`, etc.), create systemd service files, and set up configuration files in `/etc/`. No files are modified outside the build or package directories.

**No malicious indicators found:** There is no use of `eval`, base64 decoding, obfuscated commands, `curl|bash`/`wget|sh` patterns, hidden network requests, data exfiltration, or backdoor installation. The `rustup install` commands download the official Rust toolchain (pinned to version 1.91.0) which is standard for Rust-based builds. All file operations are confined to standard build/installation directories.

**Minor non-security observations:** The `noextract=($pkgname-$pkgver.tgz)` line references a file not present in the source array (since `$pkgname` as a bare array reference expands to its first element only), making it a no-op leftover — this is a harmless artifact, not malicious. The `$sha256sums[0]` syntax (without braces) is a bash quirk that works but could be written more precisely as `${sha256sums[0]}`. These do not constitute security risks.
</details>
